chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn and Abū Ayyūb, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: concerning

A man who said to his wife, “O adulteress, I committed zina with you.” He عليه السلام said: “One hadd penalty is upon him for his qadhf against her. As for his statement, ‘I committed zina with you,’ there is no hadd in it unless he testifies against himself with four testimonies of zina before the Imam.”

key_terms.أَرْبَعَ شَهَادَاتٍ: four formal testimonies required for legal self-confession here
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate judicial authority before whom such testimony is made

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man says to his wife, “O adulteress, I committed zina with you”?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding a husband who accuses his wife of zina and also implicates himself. The accusation against the wife incurs the hadd of qadhf, while his self-incriminating statement alone does not establish the hadd for zina unless he formally testifies against himself four times before the Imam.
